examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Product Involving an Inverse of an Elementary 3x3 Matrix
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that $E_1$ and $E_2$ are both elementary matrices.

First, we need to find $E_1^{-1}.$ We write down $E_1$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply an elementary row operation that transforms the left matrix into the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}[{E}_{1}\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -11 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+11{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 11 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14058885/assets/a0abd59d726f0777ec9e6b79d9d3f08210a9671b164f8191d0cb7ab7612a0f1d.png)

Now, we can find the product $E_1^{-1} E_{2}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14058885/assets/5c23e75d988cc6e1be11f454d210431078bb2fd5735f66e21831e241f43be764.png)

feedback.problem:
What is the inverse of the elementary matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply an elementary row operation that transforms the left matrix into the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse is obtained on the right-hand side of our big matrix after the transformation. Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
